newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia senator wins time to answer charges.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia senator wins time to answer charges.

text.p: Australian independent senator Mal Colston on Tuesday won extra time to account for apparent discrepancies in his travel allowances.

President of the Senate, Margaret Reid, said she had given Colston another week to respond to allegations that he had rorted his travel expenses after receiving a second report into the affair on Monday.
"Senator Colston has requested an extension of time for him to respond to both reports as he has to examine associated documents," Reid told parliament, without giving details of the second report.

"I have now asked Senator Colston to respond to both reports by no later than Monday, March 24, and I have indicated that I will table both reports in the absence of his response if it is not received by that date."

Colston, on whom the government often relies to get contentious legislation through the non-government dominated Senate, has also been accused of misusing his government car entitlements and giving office jobs to relatives who do not work.

Colston, who has previously denied all charges, is also under separate investigation by the Administrative Services Department and police are examining allegations to determine if a police investigation is warranted.
